messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a handful of runtime flags are drifting between console and the active rollout. UI shows them enabled but the runtime still serving old value. anyone else seen this?
kevin: yup saw one earlier, thought it was a cache TTL issue. did you capture an example key?
sophia: @maria can you paste the flag id? also which environment (prod/dedicated)?
maria: flag: enable_new_routing_algo_v3, env: prod-us-west. console: 60% on, runtime: 0 for a subset of hosts.
jamal: interesting — might be the propagation handshake failing on hosts behind the older agent. quick question: do we have a drift detector alerting on config skew?
tess: currently we only webhook config changes to infra events, no continuous skew detector. ops-bot: scheduled config-sanity-check ran at 2024-07-22T18:00Z — no failures reported. :robot_face:
kevin: that's the problem — the sanity check is snapshot-based and misses transient apply failures. we need a stream-based detector that compares intended config to live effective config per host.
sophia: agree. proposal: add a periodic fetch from runtime /v1/active-config and diff against console state, emit metric config.skew.count with tags (flag,env,host). alert if > 0 for 5m. simple and actionable.
maria: +1. also we should track who last changed the flag and the rollout id in the metric so SRE can triage quickly.
jamal: for rollout UX, adding the rollout id helps link to the console timeline. we should also emit a small histogram of time-to-converge per rollout.
tess: we need to be careful about cost. querying every host every minute will be noisy at scale. maybe sample hosts (pct) and only expand to full scan when skew is detected.
kevin: sampling is fine. implement two-tier detector: sampled checks (1% hosts / 1m) for early detection, and a full convergence job that runs for flagged rollouts and computes time-to-converge.
sophia: pseudocode for the detector job: ```
for rollout in active_rollouts:
  hosts = sample_hosts(rollout, pct=1)
  intended = console.get_flag_state(rollout.flag)
  live = runtime.fetch_active_config(hosts)
  diffs = diff(intended, live)
  if diffs:
    emit("config.skew.count", len(diffs), {"flag": rollout.flag, "rollout": rollout.id})
    enqueue(full_scan_job, rollout.id)
```
maria: love it. for operator handoff: when full_scan_job finds skew, we should create a slack thread in #eng-oncall with a short playbook: patch retry, restart agent, or roll back flag. keep steps minimal.
jamal: suggestion: add an "auto-rollback" toggle per rollout with a TTL guard — if skew persists for > 10m and > X% hosts, automatically rollback to previous stable. must be gated behind an approval flag for prod.
tess: scary but useful. require two approvals for auto-rollback in prod and a dry-run flag for 24h to collect telemetry first.
kevin: operational detail — store rollout TTL in the config object (e.g., rollout.ttl_seconds). console should show countdown and allow extension. also add audit-entries for each automatic action.
sophia: don't forget telemetry gating: any detector/emitter must attach hash of prompt-set (we mean rollout test-set) and a small sample of error traces (redacted) to the telemetry event. that helps QA decide whether to approve auto-rollback.
maria: action items: 1) kevin will sketch detector API and sampling plan; 2) sophia will add metric names/tag schema and full-scan job; 3) tess will draft the auto-rollback approval UX and audit trail; 4) jamal will write a short ops playbook for slack.
kevin: I'll post a short design doc in #eng-platform/design later today.
jamal: FYI — if we implement this, we can also reuse the detector for feature flag staleness (flags that never finish rollouts). win-win.
ops-bot: note: reminder to run config-sanity-check in emergency mode if skews > 10 detected — see runbook: https://confluence.local/runbooks/config-skew
tess: thanks all. small ask: can we prioritize sampling + metric first so alerts can go to SLO-oncall? low-effort, high-value.
maria: agreed. I'll schedule a 30m sync with kevin + sophia tomorrow at 10am PT. :calendar:
kevin: cool. filing the ticket now. https://rdrwd.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-4321
sophia: adding label config-skew, telemetry, rollout-ux.
maria: thanks team.
